acceptance: No shipped path requires the user to install other software manually before it can proceed.
A guard fails when a new manual-install prerequisite is added.
TPC-DI data generation obtains its Java runtime without a manual install, or TPC-DI stays unavailable until it does.
context: Raised by the owner while deciding whether the TPC-DI appendix SQL ships in the wheel (decision R2: ship it). It directly affects reopening TPC-DI, whose data generator needs Java 8.
description:
## Owner instruction (2026-11-28)
"file a follow up for enforce that we NEVER ship anything in benchbox that forces the user to install other software manually before proceeding"

## Problem
Some shipped paths stop until the user installs other software by hand. Known case: TPC-DI data generation runs the TPC's DIGen, which needs a Java 8 runtime the user must install (the TPC-DI tools bundle and DIGen source under `benchbox/core/tpcdi/`); the TPC-DI reopening is about to make that path a user path. Other benchmarks and platforms may have similar prerequisites (native tools, system libraries, servers).

## Change
1. Inventory every shipped path that requires software outside the installed Python packages before it can proceed, with the file and the check that enforces it.
2. For each: provide it automatically (a managed, pinned download or bundled runtime with checksum verification, consistent with existing binary handling), or make the path not shipped/unavailable until it can be provided.
3. Add a guard (test or lint) that fails when a new shipped path introduces a manual-install prerequisite.

## Open points for the owner
Whether a managed download at first use (with checksum and licence notice) counts as automatic; how this applies to platforms whose server the user runs themselves.
